Urban Tree Canopy Lowers Street-Level Heat by Up to 4 °C
Priya Natarajan¹, Tomás Ferreira¹, Grace Liu²
¹Department of Environmental Science, Northfield University  ·  ²Cityscape Climate Lab
Summer heat is the deadliest weather hazard in cities. Street trees cool the air through shade and evapotranspiration, but how much canopy is enough to make a measurable difference on a single block?
• Canopy cover mapped from 2025 aerial imagery
• Air temperature logged every 10 min, June–August
• Mixed-effects model controlling for pavement, building height and wind
Fig. 1 — Study area and logger locations
Fig. 2 — Mean afternoon peak by canopy cover
on blocks with more than 40% canopy versus less than 10%
Cooling grew fastest between 10% and 40% cover, then levelled off. Effects were strongest between 2 pm and 6 pm.
• Reaching 25% canopy on every block would cut peak heat by about 2 °C
• Planting priority should go to blocks under 10% cover
• Results support a city-wide canopy target in the 2027 climate plan
We are extending the logger network to 120 blocks and adding surface temperature and resident heat-stress surveys.
